Messages.Author: Thrall of Arika
Messages.Body:
Deck Name:   Tremere Blood Drive
Created By:  Thrall of Arika
Description:
Always wanted to play around with draining blood off vampires, and the
Tremere seem well equipped to do so. Main idea was to drain blood to
force vampires to hunt, catch them and burn with Marisa Fletcher, or
torporize. A couple of bad plays on my part hasn't allowed me to really
test and try this deck yet, but I think it has some potential. The main
problems I've encountered so far are pool gain, and surprisingly, blood
gain for the vampires. Rarely seem to draw into my Thefts and such when
I could really use them.

For some odd reason, I put [DECK] in the subject of my other two posts,
but they did not appear when posted.

As others have said, smallify this a bit. There are definitely some
good !Tremere you can work into the mix without screwing up all your
clan-requiring cards, as well. Hannigan, Selena and Ladislas Toth are
all very solid.

> Library: (90 cards)
> -------------------
> Master (14 cards)
>   1  Academic Hunting Ground
>   3  Blood Doll
>   1  Chantry
>   1  KRCG News Radio
>   1  Legacy of Caine
>   1  Minion Tap
>   1  Mob Connections
>   2  Strained Vitae Supply
>   2  Vampiric Disease
>   1  XTC-Laced blood

See my advice on your combat package below as to why you don't need Mob
Connections.
Strained Vitae supply should just be intercept locations, which have
the same effect when someone else is hunting and will also help you
stay alive against threats.
Vampiric Disease probably isn't worth running if you're not going to be
using permanent sources of maneuvers, as it'll come back and bite you
in the ass at some point or another.
XTC-Laced Blood is essentially a wasted slot and MPA; if you're lucky,
another one of your prey's minions will take the action to remove it,
and if you can block that, why not just block the guy hunting in the
first place? (If you're unlucky, someone will get rid of it
crosstable.)

Elder Library might be a decent replacement for some of these if you
want to keep the events.

> Action (14 cards)
>   2  Govern the Unaligned
>   3  Graverobbing
>   4  Nose of the Hound
>   4  Rutor`s Hand
>   1  Seeds of Corruption

I'm not really a fan of Rutor's Hand for a crypt like the one you've
got, but if it works for you, go for it. You can probably drop one
Graverobbing and the Seeds of Corruption.

> Reaction (15 cards)
>   2  Eagle`s Sight
>   4  Precognition
>   2  Spirit`s Touch
>   6  Forced Awakening
>   1  Poison Pill

This should be supplemented with more permanent intercept.

> Combat (38 cards)
>   2  Telepathic Tracking
>   7  Apportation
>   3  Blood to Water
>   4  Cauldron of Blood
>   2  Drain Essence
>   1  Eldritch Glimmer
>   2  Movement of the Mind
>   10 Theft of Vitae
>   3  Walk of Flame
>   4  Trap

Too much going on here, particularly for your deck. The aim of your
deck is to strip blood off your prey's minions, so stick with what
works for that. You don't need all this second-round nonsense.

10-12 Theft
10-12 Movement of the Mind
2-4 Soul Burn or Blood Fury

At the very least, this package will free up 10 slots that can be
better used for more useful stuff.

> Ally (3 cards)
>   1  Gregory Winter
>   1  Neighborhood Watch Commander (Hunter)
>   1  Procurer

With Thaumaturgy combat, Procurer is silly. Get another NWC in there
instead.

> Retainer (1 cards)
>   1  Mr. Winthrop
>
> Equipment (1 cards)
>   1  IR Goggles

There should be a .44, Bowl of Convergence, and probably Sport Bike in
here as well.

> Event (4 cards)
>   2  Dr. Marisa Fletcher, CDC
>   1  Restricted Vitae
>   1  Torpid Blood

These are pretty solid, though the handsize restrictions might hurt you
more than they're worth.


John Eno

I assume - no, by virtue of having the "unless forced to" clause on the
  prohibitive effect.

Restricted Vitae
Gehenna.
Do not replace until a vampire successfully hunts. Vampires cannot hunt
  unless forced to hunt. A vampire who must hunt may hunt by stealing a
  blood from a younger vampireas a (D) action instead of performing the
  usual hunt action.

Restricted Vitae has a different effect on vampires who are not forced
  to hunt (preventing them from hunting) and those who are forced to hunt
  (allowing them to hunt by stealing a blood from a younger vampire).

Regards,

Daneel

No, by card text. As Daneel pointed out, it's the texts that matter. 
It's not a case of simultaneously must hunt and can't hunt. It's a case 
of Restricted saying they can't hunt _unless forced to_. XTC, by it's 
explicit card text, forces them to hunt. So there's no contradiction.
